# Zettelkasten method

One idea per note, written in your own words, linked densely to other notes.
That's the whole method; everything else is tooling.

## The three note types

- **Fleeting notes**: capture, unfiltered. Inbox material.
- **Literature notes**: summaries of what you read, with the source attached.
- **Permanent notes**: one self-contained idea, written as if for a stranger.
  These live in the main sequence and get linked from everywhere relevant.

## Linking discipline

A permanent note with no incoming links is a dead end. When I file one, I
spend five minutes finding 2–3 existing notes it connects to and write the
link *with context* — a sentence explaining the relationship, not a bare
`[[link]]` at the bottom. The Luhmann-style numeric IDs are optional;
timestamps work fine as unique identifiers.

## What it changed

After a year, the surprising benefit wasn't recall — it was writing speed.
Arguments arrive pre-structured because the atomic notes already did the
thinking. The vault stops being a filing cabinet and starts being a
conversation partner.
